To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the loop closing problem can be addressed without recourse to the metric information of the SLAM problem, and (ii) loop closing can be achieved by analyzing the similarity between scene sequences

(i) the problem of detecting loop closure in a mobile mapping application is best addressed by considering the appearance of the scene rather than the metric estimates of position and orientation, (ii) the appearance of the scenes can be captured using a single camera and a laser scanner, (iii) the similarity between the scenes can be measured using a simple and efficient algorithm that is based on computing a similarity measure for each pixel in the scene and then averaging these measures to get a global measure for the scene,

loop closure in SLAM can be improved by: 1) using the appearance of scenes rather than the metric state of a robot to detect loop closure, 2) using a similarity matrix to represent the appearance of a scene, 3) using statistical analysis and remediation of the similarity matrix to improve the detection of loop closure, and 4) using a multi-robot system to improve loop closure.
